frontier.hypothesis: The h-escape chassis (7/173, latch already byte-exact) closes if global.c can be made to seat `j` in $t4 and `complement` in $t5 instead of the reverse — 6 rows, no scheduling or ordering component left.
frontier.mechanism: The carrier adds one global allocno live from the latch to the loop-exit block, which shifts the allocno-priority ordering of the two long-lived inner-loop pseudos `j` and `complement`. Note reg_n_refs on `j` is NOT the lever here: u1 removes the s21 chain extender entirely and still scores 7.
frontier.next_probe: Run `bash tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s37/qty.sh tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s37/v6/s4.c s4` (it exports BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG and BB2_QTY_DEBUG and writes -da dumps) and read the allocno priorities and hard-reg preferences of `j` and `complement`; then classify with tools/ra_solver's global.c model + inverse_compose.py classify for a typed REACHABLE/FORECLOSED verdict BEFORE spelling more C. rejected/s37-single-set-h-escape-latch-exact-t4t5-swap-7.c is the chassis.

frontier.hypothesis: A carrier that is single-set and non-block-local WITHOUT being a fresh local exists in the body, which would satisfy both predicates inside the sanctioned families rather than needing a new ruling.
frontier.mechanism: H37-1 shows the Judge-granted `total` borrow can never satisfy the order predicate because `total`'s row-top assignment is its second set — so the current candidate's 2-row residual is not closable by any spelling of that borrow. The predicate needs exactly one set in the whole function plus one reference in another basic block.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the body's variables for 'assigned exactly once and legitimately readable after the inner loop'; and test the combination this session did not reach — the guard spelled inline (f7's 27-point chassis) so that `total` itself becomes single-set at the latch, with a dominated post-loop read, to see whether the 25-point guard cost and the 5-point carrier cost overlap rather than add.

frontier.hypothesis: A byte-neutral, latch-dominated cross-block read exists whose consumer is already allocated to a register free on the latch-to-exit edge, so the carrier costs no extra allocno and the 7-chassis drops straight to 0.
frontier.mechanism: All 26 spellings measured cost the $t4/$t5 rotation because the carrier must stay live from the latch to the read. A read consumed by a pseudo that global.c already seats in the register the carrier would take (or a read GCC sinks back into the latch block after flow has recorded it) would be free.
frontier.next_probe: Widen the enumerate region to the guard block and the loop-exit block with tools/spelling_enum.py (ENUM-BEGIN/ENUM-END around `if (total > 0) { ... }` plus the first statement after the inner loop) and sweep WITH the operand-swap axis; the generators tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s37/gen6.py and gen9.py already parameterise the read target and the complement/j declarations.

judge_constraints: Remove `h`; if a staging carrier is needed, borrow the existing dead `total` under staged-value-reused-variable (per-site liveness stated in the FAKE annotation) — never a fresh multi-written local.
